title: Columbus's first voyage to the Indies, 1492–93
summary: Three ships out of Palos, a month on the trade winds from the Canaries, landfall in the Bahamas, then Cuba and Hispaniola; home on the westerlies by the Azores and Lisbon.

events.label: Landfall at Guanahaní (San Salvador)
events.source: Columbus's journal via Las Casas; Watling Island identification
events.text: A sailor, Rodrigo de Triana, called land a little after two in the morning. At daybreak Columbus went ashore, claimed the island for Castile and named it San Salvador, while the islanders, Lucayan Taíno, came down to the beach. Which island it was is still argued: Watling Island is the usual answer, with Samana Cay and others in contention.

events.label: Santa María wrecked off Hispaniola; Navidad built
events.text: On Christmas night the Santa María ran onto a reef off Hispaniola while the helmsman slept and a ship's boy held the tiller. Columbus built a small fort from her timbers, La Navidad, and left thirty-nine men in it. When he returned the next year it was burned and nobody was left.
